requirement:
The view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` MUST show
each `habeas:coverage` citation attached to the file root or an explicitly
declared function or method. Each entry MUST identify its source item and
source location and show the fenced citation commentary and Rust doc comments
supplying its tracked justification under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
When no tracked justification is present, the entry MUST say so.

File-root citations MUST be labelled as file-threshold exception proposals;
function and method citations MUST be labelled as function exception proposals,
following {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
rationale: The reviewed tests adequately cover every obligation of `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes.justifications`. All three tests are in `src/execution_coverage/notes.rs#mod[tests]`. I read `fn[entry]` and `fn[pages]` only to see what the tests render. I derived the expected behaviour from the requirement text. **Obligations and the tests that check them** 1. **Show each `habeas:coverage` citation on the file root or an explicitly declared function or method.** - `notes_show_root_function_and_method_proposals_with_owned_commentary_and_docs` uses a root citation, a free function, an `impl` method, and an unexplained function. It asserts that entries appear for `File root`, `fn[ordinary]`, `impl[Worker]/fn[work]` and `fn[unexplained]`. - The same test asserts that a citation on `mod nested` creates no file exception and that the child's docs are not shown. - `citations_on_modules_and_citation_text_in_literals_do_not_create_explanations` covers a module citation and citation text inside a string literal. It asserts that no exception proposal and no "Module only." text appear. 2. **Each entry identifies its source item and source location.** - The first test asserts the per-entry heading (`## {label}`). - For all four entries it also asserts `Source: code.rs:{first}–{last}` and `First source citation at line {citation}.` 3. **Show fenced citation commentary and Rust doc comments that supply the justification.** - The first test asserts root `//!` docs and root fenced commentary, `///` docs and fenced commentary on the function, and `/** */` docs and fenced commentary on the method. It also checks that the commentary text is HTML-escaped. - `justification_can_come_from_docs_or_fenced_commentary_but_not_ordinary_comments` checks each source on its own. Doc-only gives a "Rust doc comments" section and no "No tracked justification". Fenced-only gives a "Citation commentary" section. An ordinary comment is not shown and counts as unjustified. 4. **When no tracked justification is present, the entry says so.** - `fn[unexplained]` has only an inline `{cite}` and is asserted to say "No tracked justification is present." The test also asserts that exactly one entry says so, so justified entries do not. - The ordinary-comment case in the second test asserts the same message. 5. **Label file-root citations as file-threshold exception proposals and function or method citations as function exception proposals.** - The first test asserts exactly one "File-threshold exception proposal" and exactly three "Function exception proposal" labels. That matches the root, the function and the method, plus the unexplained function. **Residual observations (not gaps)** - A root citation with no justification is not tested on its own. It goes through the same `entry` code path, which has no root-specific justification logic. - Several citations on one item are merged into a single entry. The requirement does not distinguish this case. The tests carry `{test}` references to the subject, and I found no marking gap. No `{fixme}` acknowledgments apply.

:::{req} index.file_map.notes
Each listed first-party Rust file in the combined file coverage
map MUST provide access to a file-notes view identifying its
workspace-relative path.
:::{req} check.exceptions.anchor
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:coverage` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on a source file or explicitly declared function to propose a
> coverage exception. Explain in prose why the item's incomplete execution
> coverage is acceptable. Put the explanation in fenced citation commentary
> or Rust doc comments included in the source item's assessed input. An ordinary
> non-doc comment alone does not supply a tracked justification. The reason
> must be substantive; difficulty alone is not a justification.
> On a file's root item, the exception excuses only
> that file's 80% instrumented-line threshold, including absent measurement
> of its executable code. On an explicit function with a body, it excuses
> that function's recorded zero execution or absence from otherwise usable
> measurement, without excusing the file's threshold.
> The explanation must agree with the current source and any callers or
> configuration assumptions on which it relies. Only a current accepted
> independent assessment permits the exception. A file exception does not
> excuse unexecuted or not-measured functions in that file.
> The citation applies to its source item without conditional build matching
> and may remain when measured coverage satisfies the item's obligations.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference this built-in, inline or fenced using the standard
reference forms of {cite}`requirements.references.roles`. The built-in MUST be
available in every project without a project requirement, site query, or
exception-specific configuration.
